questions.q: In a market worth £{t}m, the three largest firms sell £{a}m, £{b}m and £{c}m. What is the 3-firm concentration ratio, in %?

options: A market dominated by a few large firms
A market with thousands of small firms
questions.why: A few firms have most of the sales, even if many small firms also exist.

questions.q: Cooperation and collusion mean the same thing.
questions.why: Collusion limits competition. Cooperation, such as on safety standards, can benefit consumers.

questions.q: Which is an example of defining oligopoly by its market STRUCTURE?
options: Firms react to each other's adverts
questions.why: Structure is about firms, shares and barriers. The others describe behaviour.

options: Act like a monopolist and maximise joint profits
questions.why: By acting together they can restrict output and raise prices.

questions.q: Explain why firms in an oligopoly face uncertainty when they change their price.

ideas.label: Firms are interdependent: one firm's move affects its rivals
It can't know how rivals will react, so it can't be sure of the result

questions.model: Firms are interdependent, so a price change affects the sales of rivals. A firm does not know how they will react, so it cannot be sure what will happen to its own sales.
questions.why: The result of your move depends on their reply.

tests.answer: Firms are interdependent, and a firm does not know how rivals will react to its price change.
